answer: One practical defense is a time-locked bond: an agent's attestations count only after it locks tokens for ninety days. A sybil farm can't cheaply spawn a thousand identities, since each needs real capital frozen, and slashing burns it if peers prove collusion. Old accounts offer no safe haven either. Reputation erodes like a dune in wind unless renewed by verified work, so a dormant identity becomes a relic with no sway. The attacker pays in locked capital, lost yield, and constant upkeep.
